title: Decision-grade ML validation: locked OOS + power-matched CPCV promotion gate + executable labels

changes.name: DECISION_LABEL_COLUMNS
changes.description: Registry of every column produced by this module (entry_close, entry_change_ratio, nd_open, nd_high, nd_low, nd_close, mechanical_gross, has_mechanical_label, label_price_ratio, cost_ratio, cost_measured, eval_net_journaled, eval_net_mechanical). Single source of truth for the look-ahead guard and for dataset._EXCLUDED_FROM_X.

changes.name: assert_no_label_leakage
changes.description: Raise ValueError naming every offending column if any DECISION_LABEL_COLUMNS member appears in feature_cols. Shipped guard for the 2026-09-06 look-ahead bug (nd_* merged into the feature matrix).

changes.name: attach_per_row_cost_ratio
changes.signature: def attach_per_row_cost_ratio(df: pd.DataFrame, *, price_col: str = 'close_price', impact_col: str | None = None, fallback_ratio: float = ROUND_TRIP_COST_RATIO) -> pd.DataFrame
changes.description: Delegate to src.execution.cost_model.estimate_round_trip_cost_bp; add cost_ratio = round_trip_cost_bp/1e4 (never NaN; per-row fail-open to fallback_ratio) and cost_measured: bool. Overwrite semantics: drop pre-existing outputs first.

changes.name: attach_mechanical_return
changes.signature: def attach_mechanical_return(df: pd.DataFrame, price_history_df: pd.DataFrame, *, date_col: str = 'trade_date', code_col: str = 'stock_code') -> pd.DataFrame
changes.description: Delegate to src.ml.exit_policy.attach_next_day_path, then add mechanical_gross = nd_open/entry_close - 1 (both legs from price_history, so back-adjustment cancels), has_mechanical_label: bool, and label_price_ratio = close_price/entry_close for adjustment provenance.

changes.name: build_decision_labels
changes.signature: def build_decision_labels(processed: pd.DataFrame, price_history_df: pd.DataFrame | None, *, label_mode: str, cost_mode: str, clip_lower: float, clip_upper: float) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, Any]]
changes.description: Compose cost + labels. Always emits cost_ratio and unclipped eval_net_journaled = net_return/100 - cost_ratio. With price history, also emits mechanical_gross and eval_net_mechanical. target_return = clip(eval_net_<label_mode>, clip_lower, clip_upper). label_mode='mechanical' drops rows lacking a mechanical label. Returns (labelled_df, provenance).

changes.name: ValidationConfig
changes.description: Fields: oos_reserve_start: str (required), eval_col: str = 'eval_net_mechanical', cpcv_n_groups: int = 8, cpcv_k_test: int = 2, purge_gap: int = 1, promotion_alpha: float = 0.05, min_ic_path_win_rate: float = 0.75, min_top1_path_win_rate: float = 0.60, min_selection_dsr: float = 0.95, min_oos_days: int = 60, min_oos_rank_ic: float = 0.0, require_fillable_sleeve: bool = True, target_notional_100m: float = 0.5. __post_init__ fail-closed on every domain.

changes.name: GateOutcome
changes.description: Fields: name: str, passed: bool, observed: float, threshold: float, detail: dict[str, Any].

changes.name: PromotionDecision
changes.description: Fields: deployable: bool, verdict: str ('deployable'|'research_only'), failed_gates: tuple[str, ...], gates: tuple[GateOutcome, ...], evidence: dict[str, Any].

changes.name: minimum_detectable_effect
changes.signature: def minimum_detectable_effect(sd: float, n_obs: int, *, alpha: float = 0.05, power: float = 0.80) -> float
changes.description: (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_power) * sd / sqrt(n_obs). Raise on sd<=0 or n_obs<1. Attached to every gate so a null result is labelled underpowered rather than negative.

changes.name: paired_t_p_value
changes.description: Two-sided one-sample t-test p-value on the paired daily difference; raise on non-finite input or n<2. Analytic cross-check on the moving-block bootstrap.

requirements: R1 (locked OOS, fail-closed): production publish is impossible without a locked window. `publish_bundle` writes to production_dir only when `decision.deployable`; `retrain.py` rejects `--publish` without `--oos-reserve-start`; `ChampionTuningConfig` rejects a `validation` config whose `oos_reserve_start` is None or disagrees with its own. The reserved window is split off before HPO, feature selection, blend-weight search and policy selection (the existing `split_oos` + `assert_oos_excluded` pair already enforces this and must keep guarding `dev` and `control_dev`).

R2 (score-once): `evaluate_locked_oos` fits on `dev` only and scores the reserved window exactly once per retrain. It raises when `oos_df` is empty or shares any group value with `dev_df`. No tuning, threshold, weight or feature decision may read the returned dict.

R3 (power-matched statistics): every gate carries the MDE of its own statistic. Gates that decide promotion are stated on rank-IC (measured daily sd 0.2745 -> MDE 0.049 at 244 OOS days, resolvable); top-1 mean net (measured daily sd 4.667%/day -> MDE 0.83%/day at 244 days, not resolvable) is used only as a sign-consistency check and must never be gated on a p-value at OOS scale. `GateOutcome.detail` records the MDE so a failing gate reads 'underpowered', not 'no effect'.

R4 (conservative significance): the dev-period significance gate uses `max(p_bootstrap, p_paired_t)`. The moving-block bootstrap CI on the shipped 2026-09-03 champion implies se 0.074%/day against an analytic 0.100%/day on n=2,175 paired days; the gate must not inherit the tighter of two disagreeing estimators.

R5 (honest selection budget): `deflated_sharpe_ratio` is computed with `n_independent_trials = hpo_trials * len(p_good_weight_grid) * len(policy_candidates)` (>= 600 at current defaults), not `search.n_trials` alone, and gates at `min_selection_dsr`. A None DSR fails the gate; it may never pass silently.

R6 (path consistency, split by power): `cpcv_ic_path_win_rate >= 0.75` and `cpcv_top1_path_win_rate >= 0.60` over the CPCV(8,2) 28 test-bin combinations. A 'path' here is one test-bin combination, matching the shipped `ExitRuleResult.cpcv_path_deltas` vocabulary.

R7 (executable label): `eval_net_mechanical = nd_open/entry_close - 1 - cost_ratio` is the promotion metric. Both price legs come from `price_history_df`, so per-symbol back-adjustment (measured: the close_price/entry_close ratio is a per-symbol constant, median within-symbol CV 0.0004, 33% of rows affected) cancels exactly. Never mix a trade-log close with a price-history open in one ratio.

R8 (per-row cost): with `cost_mode='per_row'`, `cost_ratio` comes from `estimate_round_trip_cost_bp` (statutory 20bp + KRX 2-tick spread + measured auction impact). Measured dispersion on the real panel is p10 32.6bp / p50 45.2bp / p90 60.0bp against the flat 46bp constant, so cost varies by ~27bp across the cross-section -- the same order as the whole alpha. Unmeasurable rows fail open to `ROUND_TRIP_COST_RATIO`; `cost_ratio` is never NaN.

R9 (auction impact wired): `champion.py` must call `measure_auction_impact_bp` before `estimate_round_trip_cost_bp` and pass `impact_col='auction_impact_bp'`. The shipped 2026-09-03 run reported `n_impact_measured=0` because the impact producer was never invoked, silently treating the measured +9.1bp mean / 59bp sd decision-to-auction drift as zero.

R10 (fillability has gate authority): `buyability_target_notional_100m` defaults to 0.5 in the CLI so `evaluate_buyability_sleeves` actually runs (the shipped run reported `status: skipped`). The fillable sleeve is re-selected inside the OOS window and its top-1 sign gates promotion when `require_fillable_sleeve`. `measured_share` is recorded on every sleeve claim.

R11 (look-ahead guard shipped): `assert_no_label_leakage` runs on `feature_cols` immediately after `build_ml_dataset` and again after `select_stable_features`, and `dataset._EXCLUDED_FROM_X` is extended with `DECISION_LABEL_COLUMNS`. This closes the 2026-09-06 bug where `attach_next_day_path` outputs entered the feature matrix and produced a phantom Sharpe 1.69 that collapsed to -0.15 once removed.

R12 (behaviour preservation): `label_mode='journaled'` + `cost_mode='flat'` must reproduce `retarget_with_clip` bit-for-bit, and `config.validation is None` must leave `train_tuned_champion_bundle` on its existing walk-forward path. Every currently passing test in tests/unit/ml must keep passing unchanged.

R13 (candidate artifact always written): a research_only verdict still writes the candidate bundle to `_candidate_export_dir` with `bundle['promotion_decision']` attached. Only the production root is gated. `promotion_record.json` exists exactly when a publish happened.

R14 (experiment protocol -- the ML lever): after implementation, run three full retrains with identical CPCV folds, identical seeds and the same locked window `--oos-reserve-start 2025-09-01` (~244 reserved trading days, dev 2016-01-04..2025-08-29): (a) `--label-mode journaled --cost-mode flat` (incumbent baseline), (b) `--label-mode journaled --cost-mode per_row`, (c) `--label-mode mechanical --cost-mode per_row`. Record ic_candidate, ic_path_win_rate, top1_path_win_rate, oos_rank_ic, oos_top1_mean, fillable top1_mean and measured_share for each into docs/results/ml-res.md. Prior evidence for (c): retargeting to the mechanical label moved rank-IC +0.0375 (p<1e-4) holding in 27/28 CPCV folds. Run each to completion -- no shortened date range, no reduced HPO trial count, no timeout (.agents/rules/performance.md section 0).

R16 (auditable gate logging): `run_promotion_gate` emits one `[EVAL]` line per gate in the project tag schema -- `[EVAL] gate=<name> passed=<bool> observed=%.4f threshold=%.4f mde=%.4f` -- plus a single `[EVAL] verdict=<verdict> failed_gates=<n>` summary, and `publish_bundle` emits `[SYS] stage=publish published=<bool> production_dir=<path>`. Floats at 3-4 decimals; no collections in the message body (.agents/rules/logging.md).

R15 (expected direction, stated up front): headline top-1 numbers are expected to FALL under (c) because the journaled label carries operator exit skill that a mechanical execution will not reproduce (same predictions score IC 0.20 journaled vs 0.11 mechanical). The improvement claimed by this spec is rank-IC on the label that is actually executable plus an OOS-confirmed portion -- not a higher paper top-1. A run whose paper top-1 rises while oos_rank_ic stays under its MDE must be reported as research_only.

design_rationale.alternatives_considered: (1) Keep the walk-forward bootstrap gate and just lower promotion_alpha -- rejected: the p-value is computed on the same OOF that HPO, feature selection, blend weight and policy candidate all maximised, so tightening alpha shrinks nothing that is actually being controlled. (2) Gate on an OOS top-1 significance test -- rejected on power: measured paired daily top-1 sd is 4.667%/day, giving MDE 0.83%/day over a 244-day window, so such a gate would reject every real effect this project can produce; rank-IC (sd 0.2745, MDE 0.049) is the only statistic the available window can resolve. (3) Wait for more data -- rejected and already quantified: 10.8 years for a 25bp/day top-1 effect. (4) Re-introduce rule-based selection filters (change-rate rank, cost rank, top-K) -- rejected: all were invalidated on 2026-09-06 as artifacts of the nd_* look-ahead bug (Sharpe 1.69 -> -0.15). (5) Put publish logic in bundle.py -- rejected: validation.py imports fit_seed_ensemble from bundle.py, so the reverse edge would be a cycle. (6) Flip the ChampionTuningConfig defaults to mechanical/per_row -- rejected: it would silently change every existing caller and test; the CLI defaults carry the new production path instead, and the A/B is run explicitly under R14.
design_rationale.chosen_reason: The current pipeline can only produce paper numbers: it selects and tests on one OOF (oos_row_count=0), scores on a label containing discretionary operator exit timing, charges one flat cost to every name, reports fillability and auction impact as provenance with no gate authority, publishes to production by manual copy, and quotes a saturated DSR computed against 1/15th of its real search budget. This spec makes each of those a fail-closed gate with an MDE attached, so the pipeline's own output states whether a bundle is deployable or research-only. The ML lever is placed on the label rather than on the model: training and scoring on nd_open/entry_close (the operator's actual mechanical execution) net of per-row cost is the one change with independent prior evidence (rank-IC +0.0375, p<1e-4, 27/28 CPCV folds) and it simultaneously removes the discretionary component that made every prior number unusable for a real allocation decision.
failure_modes: Silent label downgrade: price_history is missing or stale, label_mode='mechanical' falls back to the journaled label, and the gate scores the very quantity it was built to exclude. Guarded by R1/R7 -- build_decision_labels raises rather than substituting, and rows without nd_open are dropped with the loss in provenance (measured coverage 99.68%, so a sudden drop is a data alarm).

Look-ahead recurrence: attach_next_day_path outputs re-enter feature_cols through a new code path (exactly the 2026-09-06 bug: phantom Sharpe 1.69 -> -0.15). Guarded by R11 -- DECISION_LABEL_COLUMNS is the single registry feeding both dataset._EXCLUDED_FROM_X and assert_no_label_leakage, called before every fit.

Adjustment mismatch: mixing the trade log's raw close_price with price_history's back-adjusted next open would inject a per-symbol constant factor into the label (33% of rows affected, ratios spanning 0.2x-9x). Guarded by R7 -- both legs of mechanical_gross come from price_history; label_price_ratio is recorded as provenance only and never enters a return calculation.

Gate theatre: gates that can never fail (a saturated DSR of 1.0, a fillable sleeve reporting status=skipped, an auction impact of exactly zero from n_impact_measured=0) make the verdict meaningless. Guarded by R5/R9/R10 -- the DSR trial count includes the whole selection budget, a None DSR fails, the impact producer is wired in, and the sleeve evaluator is enabled by CLI default.

OOS window contamination via panel restoration: build_restored_trade_log synthesises rows from price_history, so a restored row inside the reserved window is still legitimately out-of-sample for the model but its journaled label is synthetic. Mitigated by R7 -- the promotion metric is the mechanical label, which is identically defined for journaled and restored rows.

Underpowered null read as a negative: an OOS rank-IC of 0.02 against an MDE of 0.049 means 'cannot tell', not 'no skill'. Guarded by R3 -- every GateOutcome.detail carries its MDE, and the failing gate is named oos_rank_ic_above_mde.

performance_budget.expected_data_scale: Panel: 36,744 rows after scenario_action + restoration, 33,547 after ceiling exclusion, ~61 features, 2,615 trade dates (2016-01-04..2026-08-25). Locked OOS at 2025-09-01 reserves ~244 dates / ~4,000 rows. price_history: 5,454,300 rows x 19 cols. Added compute per retrain: CPCV(8,2) = 28 folds x 2 arms = 56 LGBM fits on ~25k x 61, plus a 5-seed dev-only ensemble for the locked window. Incumbent full run is 810s; expect roughly 2-4x that.
performance_budget.storage_format: Parquet via pyarrow. Read price_history with columns=['symbol','date','open','high','low','close','daily_change_pct'] only -- attach_next_day_path copies and sorts the whole frame, so passing all 19 columns costs ~800MB for 7 that are used.
performance_budget.dtype_precision: float64 throughout for returns, costs and labels: the gate discriminates differences at bp scale (46bp cost against an 18-33bp pooled edge) and float32 rounding is ~1e-7 relative, which is fine numerically but the arrays are small enough that there is no reason to trade it. LGBM feature matrices stay as they are today.
performance_budget.chunking_strategy: None. CPCV folds run sequentially, one LGBM fit per fold per arm; the panel is ~34k rows and fits in memory whole. attach_next_day_path performs one groupby-shift over price_history followed by one left merge -- do it once per retrain and reuse the result, never per fold.

assumptions: A1: The locked OOS window is 2025-09-01 onward (~244 trading dates), chosen because it is the only period with measurable entry-day auction liquidity (2025 coverage 33%, 2026 100%), so the fillable-sleeve gate is meaningful there. The operator may override with --oos-reserve-start; below min_oos_days=60 the gate fails closed.

A2: The operator's real execution is buy ~15:19 continuous trading (approximately the entry close) and sell ~09:00+ next-day continuous trading, so nd_open/entry_close - 1 is the mechanically reproducible return. Operator-confirmed 2026-09-06; do not re-derive it.

A3: price_history is back-adjusted while the trade log holds raw traded prices. Verified this session: the close_price/entry_close ratio is a per-symbol constant (median within-symbol CV 0.0004; 59% of symbols with >=5 rows have CV < 0.02) and the exact-match share rises monotonically with recency (2019 55% -> 2025 85%), the signature of cumulative back-adjustment. Ratio labels are therefore unaffected; tick-size costing correctly uses the raw close_price.

A4: change_rate (trade log) and daily_change_pct (price_history) agree within 0.5pp on only 73% of rows even though daily change ratios should be adjustment-invariant. This is a pre-existing data-integrity question, out of scope here; build_decision_labels records the agreement share in provenance so it is visible, and no label depends on it.
A5: Existing tests in tests/unit/ml define the incumbent behaviour contract. R12 requires all of them to keep passing without modification.

scenarios.expected_behavior: Every row carries a finite cost_ratio; unusable prices fall back to the flat constant with cost_measured=False, and tradable rows disperse away from the constant.
scenarios.test_skeleton:
def test_attach_per_row_cost_ratio_falls_back_on_bad_price() -> None:
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from src.ml.decision_labels import attach_per_row_cost_ratio
    from src.serving.realtime.inference import ROUND_TRIP_COST_RATIO

    # Given two tradable closes and two unusable ones
    df = pd.DataFrame({"close_price": [1500.0, 30000.0, np.nan, 0.0]})

    out = attach_per_row_cost_ratio(df)

    # Then no row is ever NaN-costed and unmeasurable rows fall back to the flat constant
    assert np.isfinite(out["cost_ratio"].to_numpy(dtype=float)).all()
    assert out["cost_measured"].tolist() == [True, True, False, False]
    assert np.isclose(out["cost_ratio"].iloc[2], ROUND_TRIP_COST_RATIO)
    assert np.isclose(out["cost_ratio"].iloc[3], ROUND_TRIP_COST_RATIO)
    # 1,500원 -> tick 1원 -> 2-tick round trip 13.33bp + 20bp statutory
    assert np.isclose(out["cost_ratio"].iloc[0], (20.0 + 2.0 * 1.0 / 1500.0 * 1e4) / 1e4)
    # 30,000원 -> tick 50원 -> 33.33bp + 20bp statutory
    assert np.isclose(out["cost_ratio"].iloc[1], (20.0 + 2.0 * 50.0 / 30000.0 * 1e4) / 1e4)
    # The point of per-row costing: identical picks do not carry identical cost
    assert not np.isclose(out["cost_ratio"].iloc[0], out["cost_ratio"].iloc[1])

scenarios.expected_behavior: label_mode='journaled' + cost_mode='flat' reproduces retarget_with_clip bit-for-bit, so the incumbent champion path is behaviour-preserved.
scenarios.test_skeleton:
def test_build_decision_labels_flat_journaled_matches_retarget_with_clip() -> None:
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from src.ml.dataset import retarget_with_clip
    from src.ml.decision_labels import build_decision_labels

    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "trade_date": pd.to_datetime(["2024-01-02", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-03"]),
        "stock_code": ["000001", "000002", "000001"],
        "net_return": [3.0, -50.0, 40.0],
        "target_return": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
        "close_price": [1500.0, 30000.0, 1500.0],
    })

    legacy = retarget_with_clip(df, -0.10, 0.10)
    out, prov = build_decision_labels(
        df, None, label_mode="journaled", cost_mode="flat", clip_lower=-0.10, clip_upper=0.10
    )

    # Then the legacy training label is reproduced exactly
    assert np.allclose(
        out["target_return"].to_numpy(dtype=float), legacy["target_return"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    )
    # And the unclipped evaluation label is exposed alongside it
    assert np.isclose(out["eval_net_journaled"].iloc[2], 40.0 / 100.0 - out["cost_ratio"].iloc[2])
    assert prov["label_mode"] == "journaled"
    assert prov["cost_mode"] == "flat"
    assert prov["n_rows"] == 3

scenarios.expected_behavior: Fail-closed: the mechanical label cannot be silently downgraded to the journaled one when price history is absent.
scenarios.test_skeleton:
def test_build_decision_labels_mechanical_requires_price_history() -> None:
    import pandas as pd
    import pytest

    from src.ml.decision_labels import build_decision_labels

    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "trade_date": pd.to_datetime(["2024-01-02"]),
        "stock_code": ["000001"],
        "net_return": [3.0],
        "target_return": [0.0],
        "close_price": [1500.0],
    })

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="price_history"):
        build_decision_labels(
            df, None, label_mode="mechanical", cost_mode="per_row", clip_lower=-0.10, clip_upper=0.10
        )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="label_mode"):
        build_decision_labels(
            df, None, label_mode="operator", cost_mode="flat", clip_lower=-0.10, clip_upper=0.10
        )
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="cost_mode"):
        build_decision_labels(
            df, None, label_mode="journaled", cost_mode="guess", clip_lower=-0.10, clip_upper=0.10
        )

scenarios.expected_behavior: The mechanical label is next-day open over entry-day close, both read from price_history (adjustment-invariant), minus the per-row cost.
scenarios.test_skeleton:
def test_build_decision_labels_mechanical_prices_next_open_over_entry_close() -> None:
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from src.ml.decision_labels import attach_mechanical_return, build_decision_labels

def test_minimum_detectable_effect_matches_closed_form() -> None:
    import numpy as np
    import pytest
    from scipy.stats import norm

    from src.ml.validation import minimum_detectable_effect

    expected = (norm.ppf(0.975) + norm.ppf(0.80)) * 4.667 / np.sqrt(250.0)
    assert np.isclose(minimum_detectable_effect(4.667, 250), expected)

    # Measured project noise: top-1 sd 4.667%/day, daily rank-IC sd 0.2745
    assert minimum_detectable_effect(4.667, 250) > 0.25  # 25bp/day is unresolvable
    assert minimum_detectable_effect(0.2745, 250) < 0.10  # a 0.10 rank-IC is resolvable

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="n_obs"):
        minimum_detectable_effect(4.667, 0)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="sd"):
        minimum_detectable_effect(0.0, 250)

def test_evaluate_locked_oos_rejects_dev_overlap_and_scores_once() -> None:
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd
    import pytest

    from src.ml.validation import evaluate_locked_oos

    rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
    days = pd.to_datetime(pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=180, freq="D"))
    rows = 5

    def _panel(dates: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
        n = len(dates) * rows
        f1 = rng.normal(size=n)
        f2 = rng.normal(size=n)
        eval_net = 0.02 * f1 + rng.normal(scale=0.01, size=n)
        return pd.DataFrame({
            "trade_date": np.repeat(dates.to_numpy(), rows),
            "stock_code": [f"{i % 50:06d}" for i in range(n)],
            "f1": f1,
            "f2": f2,
            "target_return": eval_net,
            "eval_net_mechanical": eval_net,
        })

    dev = _panel(days[:150])
    oos = _panel(days[150:])

    result = evaluate_locked_oos(
        dev, oos, ["f1", "f2"], "target_return", "eval_net_mechanical", "trade_date",
        model_params={"n_estimators": 20, "num_leaves": 7}, huber_delta=0.9, seeds=(13, 29),
    )

    assert result["n_days"] == 30
    assert result["n_rows"] == 30 * rows
    assert np.isfinite(result["top1_mean"])
    assert np.isfinite(result["rank_ic"])
    assert -1.0 <= result["rank_ic"] <= 1.0
    assert np.isfinite(result["mde_ic"]) and result["mde_ic"] > 0.0
    assert str(result["first_date"])[:10] == "2024-05-30"

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="overlap"):
        evaluate_locked_oos(
            dev, dev, ["f1", "f2"], "target_return", "eval_net_mechanical", "trade_date",
            model_params={"n_estimators": 20}, huber_delta=0.9, seeds=(13,),
        )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="oos_reserve_start"):
